fields.h1: Build a Liability Waiver Form Every Participant Signs Online
fields.hero_description: Describe the activity and what can go wrong. Emergent builds the liability waiver form, sends a signing link to each participant and keeps every signed copy in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Liability Waiver Form
fields.features_subheading: Six parts every signed waiver depends on: the clauses, the people who sign and the record you keep afterward.
fields.feature_1:
Risk clauses the signer initials

Emergent lays out the activity, its named hazards, the assumption of risk and the release of claims as separate clauses. Each one gets an initials box before the signature line.
fields.feature_2:
A guardian section for anyone under 18

Ask for a date of birth first. A minor gets a section for the parent or guardian with name, relationship, phone and signature, and the child's record links back to that adult.
fields.feature_3:
Signatures drawn on any screen

Signers draw with a finger or a mouse. Emergent stamps the date and time, writes the signature into a PDF of the waiver and emails that copy to the signer for their own records.
fields.feature_4:
One waiver per person, never per group

Each adult in a party gets their own signing link, even when one person booked for the whole group. The booking shows who has signed and who still has to before anyone starts.
fields.feature_5:
A record staff can search at check-in

Each signed waiver becomes a row holding the signer and the date it expires. Staff look up a name at the front desk and open the signed PDF from that same row in one click.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Publish the waiver on your own domain, or put a QR code at the front desk that opens it. Export the full code to GitHub when a developer wants waivers inside your booking system.

fields.usecase_heading: Liability Waivers Built Around the Activity
fields.tab_content_1:
Kayaks stay tied up until every renter signs

Cedar Lake Paddle emails a waiver link to each adult on a booking the moment it is made. Renters initial the capsize and cold-water clauses on their phones, then sign. Staff hand over the paddles once booking #2318 shows all three renters signed. No clipboard changes hands at the dock.
fields.tab_content_2:
Six unsigned names, flagged a day before the cleanup

The Riverbend cleanup on Saturday has 40 volunteers signed up. By Friday at 9 am, 34 have signed the waiver, and the other six get a reminder by email. Those six names also post to the crew's Slack channel, where the coordinator checks who to stop at the sign-in table.
fields.tab_content_3:
Send every climber under 18 to a guardian signature

Pine Hollow Adventure Park asks for each climber's date of birth before anything else. A climber under 18 gets a guardian section with name, relationship and phone, and the parent signs for the child. Adults sign for themselves and never see that section.
fields.tab_content_4:
Site access tied to a current insurance certificate

Contractors working at Alder Street Lofts sign the building's waiver and upload a certificate of insurance before their first visit. Each certificate's end date lands in a table of every vendor. When one is within 30 days of expiring, that contractor gets an email asking for a new certificate.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Liability Waiver Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work happens before the first field is built, while you settle the hazards and who signs.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the hazards one by one
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add what staff need on the day
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what participants will do and what can go wrong: a capsized boat, a fall from a ladder, heat exhaustion on a long trail. Specific hazards read more clearly than a catch-all line about inherent risks, and each becomes a clause the signer initials.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the business and its owners, then add employees, contractors and any landowner whose property you use. Writing employees as a group instead of naming each person keeps the release accurate as staff come and go.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Settle the signing rules for groups and families before you build. Decide whether one guardian may cover several siblings in a single submission, and whether a school trip needs a form from each parent. These rules shape the form more than any field does.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Beyond the release, collect an emergency contact and any medical conditions the instructor should know about. Ask for an email address too, because the signed copy and every reminder go there. Leave out anything staff will never read on the day.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your release text word for word and describe the fields around it. Emergent builds the form with its initials boxes and signature step, plus a table of signed waivers. Change any clause later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set how long a signature lasts
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick one term and write it into the waiver, such as 12 months from the date it was signed. Emergent stores that expiry on each record and emails the signer when a new signature is due.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Have a lawyer read it, then test
fields.howto_step_7_des: Vague language is a common reason waivers fail. Ask an attorney to review the text before the first real participant sees it. Then sign it yourself as a made-up participant, open the PDF and check every initials box came through.

claims_to_source: Each adult signs their own waiver, since a family member cannot sign away another person's rights, and a parent or legal guardian signs for a minor
A waiver should name the parties it releases (owners, employees, contractors) and describe the specific hazards of the activity
A waiver can fail when its language is vague, and state laws may require specific wording or limit what can be waived
Notarization is not always required for a release form, though it can add a layer of protection
Businesses should work with legal counsel to draft a liability waiver, enforceability depends on state law, and a parent's signature for a child may not hold in every state
The California Department of Food and Agriculture publishes a Release and Waiver of Liability Agreement as a free PDF
